record.original_question: Are higher-dimensional black holes stable under perturbations, and if not, what instabilities and end states arise in the nonlinear regime?

evidence.quote: Problem P10: Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider vacuum solutions of the Einstein equations in $D \geq 5$ spacetime dimensions describing asymptotically flat or asymptotically Kaluza–Klein stationary black holes (including, e.g., Schwarzschild–Tangherlini black holes, Myers–Perry rotating black holes, black strings $\mathrm{Sch}_{D-1} \times \mathbb{R}$, black rings with horizon topology $S^1 \times S^{D-3}$, and multi-horizon configurations such as black Saturns). For each such solution, determine whether it is stable under small perturbations of the metric:

(a) Establish linear (mode) stability or instability of the solution under gravitational perturbations preserving the asymptotic conditions.
(b) When linear instability is present (e.g., the Gregory–Laflamme mode for sufficiently thin black strings, ultra-spinning Myers–Perry black holes, thin black rings), establish nonlinear instability rigorously and identify the final (end-state) configuration of the nonlinear evolution: does the horizon pinch off in finite asymptotic time leading to a naked singularity (violating weak cosmic censorship in $D \geq 5$), settle into a non-uniform stationary black object, or fragment into multiple black holes?
(c) For solutions believed to be stable (e.g., the higher-dimensional Schwarzschild–Tangherlini black hole), prove full nonlinear asymptotic stability of the family under small perturbations of initial data.

Provide a complete classification of stability and end-states for the known higher-dimensional stationary black-hole solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is broadly open. Linear Gregory–Laflamme instability of thin black strings has been rigorously established mathematically (e.g., Moschidis 2021 in J. Math. Phys.), and numerical simulations of the full Einstein equations indicate that the nonlinear evolution of unstable black strings produces a self-similar cascade pinching off in finite asymptotic time, suggesting violation of weak cosmic censorship in $D\geq 5$. However, complete nonlinear stability of higher-dimensional Schwarzschild–Tangherlini, Myers–Perry, and black ring solutions, and rigorous identification of end-states for unstable cases, remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Gregory–Laflamme instability of the Schwarzschild black string exterior
status_evidence.snippet: A direct rigorous mathematical proof of the Gregory–Laflamme instability for the five-dimensional Schwarzschild black string has been presented.
status_evidence.claim: Linear GL instability rigorously proved for 5D Schwarzschild black string.

status_evidence.title: Final state of Gregory–Laflamme instability
status_evidence.snippet: To capture the late-time nonlinear dynamics requires numerical solution of the full Einstein equations.
status_evidence.claim: End-state of GL instability remains studied numerically; full nonlinear classification incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Black Holes in Higher Dimensions (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Many higher dimensional spacetimes such as black rings, ultraspinning Myers–Perry black holes and black Saturns are inferred to be unstable.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of various higher-dimensional black objects is conjectural and partly open.
